To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the peripheral blood of patients with mycosis fungoids contains an increased percentage of OKT 4 + T cells, that this expansion is not dependent on the clinical stage of the disease and that the OKT 4+ cell expansion in MF patients is similar to that observed in other lymphoproliferative disorders, such as Sezary syndrome and cutaneous T cell lymphoma.
in patients with mycosis fungoids, there is an increase in the number of circulating T helper cells, as measured using monoclonal antibodies.
the OKT4+ T lymphocyte subset is expanded in peripheral blood of MF patients, but not in other T cell lymphomas, and that this finding suggests that MF could be a helper T lymphocyte neoplasm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of monoclonal antibodies to characterize the phenotype of peripheral blood lymphocytes from patients with mycosis fungoids (MF).
the use of monoclonal antibodies in the study of T cell subsets in MF patients.
the use of the OKT series monocloals in the study of peripheral blood lymphocytes in 16 MF patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OKT4+ helper T cells are the predominant cell in MF.
in the peripheral blood of MF patients there is an increase of the OKT4+ T cells, and that this is a constant finding in all stages of the disease.
the OKT4+ subset is expanded in MF patients, that the percentage of OKTs+ cells is in normal range, and that the percentage of the OKT8+ subset is not increased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OKT4+ subset is expanded in peripheral blood of MF patients and the OKT8+ subset is expanded within the skin of MF patients.
